name: Improved clinch knot
use: The everyday hook-to-line knot. Matt's first knot.
steps: Pass the tag end through the hook eye.
Make five turns around the standing line.
Bring the tag back through the small loop by the eye, then through the larger loop you just made.
Wet it and pull the turns snug against the eye.

name: Non-slip loop knot
use: Leaves an open loop at the lure eye so a Bagley Mullet or a spoon can swing freely.
steps: Tie a loose overhand knot in the line, pass the tag through the lure eye and back through the overhand.
Wrap the tag around the standing line; lighter line takes more wraps.
Bring the tag back through the overhand opening on the same side it left.
Wet it and tighten, keeping the loop open at the eye.

name: Uni knot
use: Line to swivel. Two of them back to back join line to leader.
steps: Pass the line through the swivel eye and double it back.
Form a loop and start wrapping the tag around both strands inside it.
Make five turns inside the loop.
Wet it, tighten the knot, then slide it down to the eye.

name: Palomar knot
use: The strongest simple hook knot. Good for the forged hooks on the boat poles.
steps: Pass a doubled loop of line through the hook eye.
Tie a loose overhand knot with the doubled line.
Pass the whole hook through the loop.
Wet it and draw everything down evenly to the eye.

name: Albright knot
use: Main line to a heavier leader, the way Matt rigs the thirty-pound leader for the big snook.
steps: Fold the heavy leader and pass the lighter line through the fold.
Wrap the light line back over itself and both strands of the fold.
After ten wraps, pass the tag back through the fold beside where it came in.
Wet it and tighten the wraps carefully.
